title: Story 16: Agent Creates Out-of-Scope Idea While Working
pmResponse:
# Action Plan — Ideas Loop Triage of #131

## Analysis

**Loop:** Ideas Loop (interleaved with the active Work Loop on #130).

**Key determinations:**
1. **#130 ("Implement checkout screen") is untouched.** It's `in-progress` under `android-developer`. The idea #131 is a separate issue. I do NOT touch #130 — the developer continues their active work.
2. **#131 is an `idea`** created by `android-developer` — a worker, **not a manager** (not team-lead / product-owner / cto / PM). So the auto-accept rule does **not** apply. This must go through a routed review.
3. **Duplicate check:** none found (per scenario). Documented in a comment.
4. **Classification:** "Add screen reader support to all screens" is a **product/UX idea** — accessibility is a product-direction decision affecting all users. Per routing rules, product/UX ideas → **`product-owner`**. It is *not* a backend technical idea (so not `backend-architect`) and it is not cross-team.
5. **Outcome depends on the product-owner's decision** — I do **not** evaluate the idea myself. I route it and get woken by a sync tracker when they decide.

**Standard ideas-loop pattern applied:** Review task (tag `task`, routed manager) + "Check review decision" sync tracker (tag `task,sync`, me) blocked by the Review.

---

## Phase A — Immediate Triage (run now, in this order)

### A1. Document the triage decision on the idea
```bash
agt comments add 131 --content "Triage: Duplicate check complete — no existing idea/issue found for 'screen reader' or 'accessibility'. Classification: this is a product/UX idea (accessibility is a product-direction decision affecting all users), so routing to product-owner for review. Android-developer continues active work on #130 (checkout screen) — unaffected. Created a Review task for product-owner and a sync tracker to wake me on the decision."
```
*Reasoning:* Every intervention gets a documented comment. Records the duplicate-check result and the routing rationale so the audit trail is complete.

### A2. Create the Review task (the decision step) under #131
```bash
agt create "Review idea: Add screen reader support to all screens" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee product-owner \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 131 \
  --description "Evaluate the accessibility idea raised by android-developer (no screens currently have proper content descriptions for screen readers; observed during checkout work on #130). Decide whether to ACCEPT (we will build it), PARK (defer), or DISCARD. Post your decision + rationale as a comment on this task. If accepting, note any scope/priority guidance for the implementation."
# → assume this returns <REVIEW>
```
*Reasoning:* The ideas loop requires a Review task tagged `task` assigned to the routed manager. Status `todo` so the work loop hands it to `product-owner`. Parent is #131 (the idea). I do NOT decide acceptance myself — the product-owner does.

### A3. Create the "Check review decision" sync tracker under #131
```bash
agt create "Check product-owner review decision on accessibility idea" \
  --tags task,sync \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 131
# → assume this returns <SYNC-TRIAGE>
```
*Reasoning:* This is my completion alarm. Tag is exactly `task,sync` (the only valid two-word tag). Assignee is me. Status `todo` (never `in-progress`). It will stay blocked while the Review is pending, so the loop does not bother me.

### A4. Block the sync tracker by the Review task
```bash
agt blockages add <SYNC-TRIAGE> --by <REVIEW>
```
*Reasoning:* The sync tracker must be blocked by the last (only) triage task. While `product-owner` works the Review, this keeps the sync tracker dormant. When they mark the Review `done`, the blockage **auto-clears** and the loop wakes me. (I never manually `blockages resolve` here.)

### A5. Take ownership of the idea parent and flip it to in-progress
```bash
agt update 131 --assignee project-manager --status in-progress
```
*Reasoning:* #131 now has children and is under active triage, so it becomes `in-progress` (mirrors the "set parent in-progress after creating children" rule). Assigning it to me makes PM ownership explicit. Because it is `in-progress` (not `todo`), the work loop will not re-wake me on it — the sync tracker is my only wake-up.

---

## Resulting Hierarchy after Phase A

```
#131 "Add screen reader support to all screens"   (tag: idea, assignee: project-manager, status: in-progress)
├── <REVIEW>  "Review idea: Add screen reader support to all screens"
│             (tag: task, assignee: product-owner, status: todo)        ← unblocked → loop hands to product-owner
└── <SYNC-TRIAGE> "Check product-owner review decision on accessibility idea"
                  (tag: task,sync, assignee: project-manager, status: todo)
                  ← BLOCKED BY <REVIEW>                                 ← dormant until Review done
```

(#130 "Implement checkout screen" remains `in-progress` under `android-developer` — untouched.)

---

## Phase B — When `<SYNC-TRIAGE>` wakes me (product-owner has decided)

First, read the decision:
```bash
agt comments list <REVIEW>
```

Then act on the branch.

### Branch 1 — ACCEPTED → retag as feature + build (frontend feature flow)

Screen reader / accessibility support is a **frontend** deliverable (content descriptions, semantic labels, focus order on Android screens). Frontend Feature phase flow: **Plan → Dev → Style → Validate**, plus a sync tracker.

```bash
# B1a. Document and close the triage sync
agt comments add <SYNC-TRIAGE> --content "Product-owner ACCEPTED. Closing triage sync. Retagging #131 as feature and standing up the implementation per the frontend feature flow (Plan → Dev → Style → Validate)."
agt update <SYNC-TRIAGE> --status done

# B1b. Retag the idea as a feature deliverable
agt update 131 --tags feature
agt comments add 131 --content "Accepted by product-owner. Retagged idea → feature. Beginning implementation."

# B1c. Phase 1 — Plan (frontend planning is done by android-developer)
agt create "Plan accessibility support across all screens" \
  --tags task --assignee android-developer --status todo --parentId 131
# → <PLAN>

# B1d. Phase 2 — Dev (android-developer implements)
agt create "Implement screen reader support (content descriptions, semantic labels)" \
  --tags task --assignee android-developer --status todo --parentId 131
# → <DEV>

# B1e. Phase 3 — Style (android-designer owns accessibility polish: focus order, Material a11y, tap targets)
agt create "Apply accessibility styling (focus order, Material a11y, tap targets)" \
  --tags task --assignee android-designer --status todo --parentId 131
# → <STYLE>

# B1f. Phase 4 — Validate (android-validator, NEVER the implementer)
agt create "Validate accessibility support across all screens" \
  --tags task --assignee android-validator --status todo --parentId 131
# → <VALIDATE>

# B1g. Sync tracker for the feature (blocked by LAST worker task = Validate)
agt create "Verify accessibility feature complete" \
  --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId 131
# → <SYNC-FEATURE>

# B1h. Chain the blockages (each phase gated on the previous; sync gated on last)
agt blockages add <DEV>      --by <PLAN>
agt blockages add <STYLE>    --by <DEV>
agt blockages add <VALIDATE> --by <STYLE>
agt blockages add <SYNC-FEATURE> --by <VALIDATE>
```

*Reasoning for Branch 1:*
- **One task per phase, never collapsed** — even though `android-developer` does both Plan and Dev, they are two separate issues.
- **Style is a separate task** for `android-designer` — accessibility polish (focus order, Material Design accessibility, tap-target sizing) is explicitly the designer's domain per the roster ("android-designer: …accessibility (AFTER developer builds)").
- **Validation is always a separate task** assigned to `android-validator`, never to the developer who built it.
- **Sync tracker blocked by the last worker task (Validate)**, not by Plan/Dev/Style. When Validate is `done`, the blockage auto-clears and I'm woken to verify and close #131.
- **#131 stays `in-progress`** (already is). Child count for the feature = 4 phases + 1 sync = **5 implementation children** (plus the 2 completed triage children), satisfying "child count = (# phase tasks) + 1."
- The Plan task is **not blocked** — acceptance is already complete when I create it, so the loop picks it up immediately.

Resulting accepted hierarchy:
```
#131 "Add screen reader support to all screens"   (tag: feature, assignee: project-manager, status: in-progress)
├── <REVIEW>      "Review idea: …"                  (done, product-owner)
├── <SYNC-TRIAGE> "Check review decision…"          (done, project-manager)
├── <PLAN>     "Plan accessibility support…"        (tag: task, android-developer, todo)   ← unblocked, starts first
├── <DEV>      "Implement screen reader support…"   (tag: task, android-developer, todo)   ← blocked by <PLAN>
├── <STYLE>    "Apply accessibility styling…"       (tag: task, android-designer, todo)    ← blocked by <DEV>
├── <VALIDATE> "Validate accessibility support…"    (tag: task, android-validator, todo)   ← blocked by <STYLE>
└── <SYNC-FEATURE> "Verify accessibility feature complete" (tag: task,sync, project-manager, todo) ← blocked by <VALIDATE>
```

### Branch 2 — DISCARDED → close
```bash
agt comments add <SYNC-TRIAGE> --content "Product-owner DISCARDED the idea. Closing triage sync and #131."
agt update <SYNC-TRIAGE> --status done

agt update 131 --tags idea,discarded --status closed
agt comments add 131 --content "Idea discarded by product-owner. Closed."
```
*Reasoning:* Discarded ideas close with the `idea,discarded` tag pair so they remain findable as rejected ideas but leave the active loop.

### Branch 3 — PARKED (deferred) — noted for completeness
```bash
agt comments add <SYNC-TRIAGE> --content "Product-owner PARKED the idea (deferred, not discarded). Closing triage sync."
agt update <SYNC-TRIAGE> --status done
agt comments add 131 --content "Parked by product-owner — deferred for future reconsideration. No implementation created. Left as an open idea for backlog visibility."
# #131 stays tag: idea, status: in-progress (NOT todo, so the loop will not re-wake me on it).
```
*Reasoning:* "Park" is not a standard terminal state in the loop. Keeping #131 at `in-progress` (never `todo`) prevents the loop from re-handing the idea to me; it remains visible in the backlog without churning the work loop.

---

## What I explicitly do NOT do

- **Do NOT touch #130** — active checkout work continues under `android-developer`.
- **Do NOT auto-accept** — the idea came from a worker (`android-developer`), not a manager.
- **Do NOT route to `backend-architect`** — this is a product/UX idea, not a backend technical idea.
- **Do NOT evaluate the idea myself** — I route to the product-owner and let their review decide.
- **Do NOT run `agt blockages resolve` in the work loop** — blockages auto-clear when the Review is marked `done`.
- **Do NOT skip the sync tracker** — both the triage and (on accept) the implementation each have their own `task,sync` child.
feedback: Excellent immediate triage matching expected Phase 1: correctly routes the product/UX idea to product-owner (explicitly not backend-architect), documents the duplicate check, creates the Review task (tag: task) and the 'Check review decision' sync tracker (tag: task,sync, assigned to project-manager, blocked by the Review). Parent #131 correctly set to in-progress and assigned to project-manager after children created; #130 left untouched so the developer's work continues undisturbed. PM explicitly does not evaluate the idea itself. One notable deviation in the agent's pre-stated Phase B plan: on acceptance it would retag #131 as `feature`, whereas the expected key behavior is to tag it `chore` (accessibility enhances existing screens, not a new capability). This is a later-phase action, so it only modestly affects behavioralAccuracy/completeness, but it conflicts with an emphasized key behavior.
